anatomy.intro: Most of the rainbow effect sits outside the green stem, in its closely arranged spines.

parts.function: Green stem tissue remains beneath the covering of spines.
parts.label: Ribbed stem

parts.function: Each small growing cushion anchors a group of radial spines.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: The closely arranged spines curve toward the stem instead of forming long outward spikes.
parts.label: Radial spine comb

parts.function: Newer spine growth near the top can be more strongly pink than older growth below.
parts.label: Crown

flowers.text: Bright pink flowers with a white throat grow from younger areoles near the top of the plant, standing above the closely packed spines.

growth.note: New spines are reddish pink; as they mature, they fade toward yellow or pale pink, creating bands of changing color down the stem.

stages.text: A small body is already covered with tightly arranged radial spines.
stages.title: Compact youngster

stages.text: The solitary stem extends upward while older spines become paler.
stages.title: Longer column

stages.text: A mature plant can carry a conspicuous pink flower near its upper areoles.
stages.title: Flowering crown

habitat.text: This subspecies comes from the Sierra Oscura of western Chihuahua, Mexico, within desert and dry shrubland. Its recorded range is much narrower than that of rainbow cacti as a whole.

image.alt: Rainbow hedgehog cactus with numbered green rib, areole, comb of pink radial spines and newer crown growth.

Echinocereus rigidissimus subsp. rubispinus, one short cylindrical rainbow hedgehog cactus. Dense close parallel comb-like radial spines lie against the stem in rows, alternating rosy pink and pale cream bands. No long projecting central spines, no branches. One small natural gap allows the green rib to be seen without cutting tissue. 1 points to a visible green vertical rib beneath the spine cover; 2 to a small spine-bearing areole; 3 to the flat comb of pink radial spines; 4 to the densely pink new growth at the apical crown.

lookalikes.name: Echinocereus rigidissimus without a subspecies label
lookalikes.text: The broader species also has closely pressed colored spines. The nursery’s subspecies label distinguishes this plant from rainbow cacti sold without that detail.

mature.text: The plant develops a solitary upright body rather than a broad mound. RHS lists a cultivated height and spread of 10–50 cm for the species.

milestones.text: Joined the collection from Costa Farms.
milestones.title: Acquired

nameStory.text: The subspecies combination dates to 1997. Kew also records older names placing it under Echinocereus pectinatus or treating rubispinus as a variety, explaining the different labels found in older references.
